title: Q4 2025 - My performance notes & manager prep
body:
Purpose: scratchpad for my end-of-year performance review, promotion discussion prep, and 2026 planning. Informal notes — will clean up before I share with manager.

Quick wins (last 12 months):
- Rolled out the new interview scorecard across Hiring Committee: 45% reduction in panel disagreements (post-rollout survey), fewer re-interviews.
- Launched People Ops onboarding checklist + LMS module: reduced new hire enablement time from avg 8 days -> 5 days (measured for eng hires).
- Led compensation calibration prep for Q3/Q4 cycles (data collection, summary deck). Helped close 3 salary band anomalies before final approvals.
- Built a lightweight offboarding playbook for Dedicated and Private sales teams (legal + infra touchpoints), now used by Sales Ops.
- Instituted monthly manager office hours (pilot) — 18 attendees avg, concrete follow-ups created (tracking doc).

Metrics I own / influenced:
- Time to productivity (eng): down 37% vs baseline 2024 (internal measure).
- Offer acceptance rate: 78% -> 84% after interview loop tweaks.
- Manager NPS (pilot): 6.8 -> 7.4 (on 10 scale) after manager office hours and toolkit.

Concrete examples / stories to call out in review:
- Interview scorecard adoption: worked cross-functionally with Eng Recruiting and Hiring Committee. Ran 3 training sessions, iterated on rubric after first 10 hires. Example: tweaked the 'system design' rubric to include ops-aware questions (helped reduce mis-hiring for infra-heavy roles).
- Onboarding LMS: Drop in enablement time came from focused 'first-week priorities' module that I wrote (scripted tasks + contact points). Solicited feedback from cohort 12 and iterated twice.
- Compensation calibrations: found an outlier case where offer comp had a calculation error; worked with finance to correct before payroll. Saved ~ $12k in incorrect payments and avoided manager escalation.

Areas for improvement / development goals (honest):
- Program management: need to tighten timelines and stakeholder comms on multi-team launches. A few pilots slipped because of misaligned expectations (not all my fault, but I can do more proactive escalation).
- Data fluency: want to get better at quickly producing dashboards (SQL + Looker skills). Currently lean on Analytics; learning to be more autonomous will speed iteration.
- Strategic influence: move from tactical PMs to helping define bigger People Ops strategy (org design, comp philosophy). Need to carve out time for higher-level thinking.

Goals for 2026 (draft):
1) Standardize onboarding for 3 non-engineering bundles (CS, Sales, Product) and cut time-to-first-impact by 20% for each.
2) Build a manager enablement program: 6 modules + practical playbook; pilot with SRE and Solutions Eng.
3) Create a quarterly people dashboard for leadership: headcount, ramp curves, offer pipeline, comp spend projections.
4) Own cross-functional incident for any hiring pipeline outages (runbook + postmortem cadence).

Signals of success / acceptance criteria:
- Onboarding: measured via new-hire survey + manager checklist completion rate >= 85% within 90 days.
- Manager program: 2 cohorts completed, improvement in manager NPS >= 0.5.
- Dashboard: weekly refresh, leadership uses it in monthly GTM + Eng reviews.

Ask for manager (to discuss in 1:1/review):
- Feedback on readiness for L5/promotion path: specific examples I should collect and behaviors to demonstrate.
- Sponsor opportunities: would appreciate being looped into 1:1s with head of Eng for co-created onboarding alignment.
- Budget for 2026: 2k for LMS content licensing + 8 hours headcount to run manager program pilot (temp contractor).
- Mentorship: ask for a quarterly 1:1 focused on org design + comp strategy (blocking on calendar).

Draft 15-min review talking points (short, can share):
- 60s: highlight 3 impact bullets (scorecards, onboarding, comp fixes).
- 3min: metrics and example story (scorecard adoption).
- 4min: 2026 goals and asks (above).
- 4min: career ask / promotion readiness + explicit next steps.

Open questions / things I want from manager:
- Is the promotion timeline realistic for H1 2026? If not, what are the concrete blockers?
- Priorities for People Ops at company level (I think: onboarding, manager enablement, comp hygiene) — does that align with your read?
- Who should I partner with to get the dashboard prioritized (analytics vs product ops)?

To-do before review (my checklist):
- Pull deck with 3 slides: Impact, metrics/examples, 2026 asks (by 2026-02-20).
- Export cohort onboarding survey results (by 2026-02-18).
- Compile 3 concrete promotion evidence examples + docs (hiring rubric, LMS module, comp case) (by 2026-02-22).
- Ask Alex to review the manager program curriculum draft (in slack).

Notes to self (phrasing + tone):
- Keep it specific and measurable. Avoid vague claims like 'improved hiring' without numbers.
- When asking for promotion, frame in terms of business outcomes and scope increase (e.g., 'I want to own manager enablement across the company' + how I'll measure).
- Be explicit about blockers I need removed, not just asks for resources.

Misc (brainstorm):
- Consider a small internal workshop (lunch + learn) on 'interview calibration' for hiring managers — 45min. Could be first deliverable of manager enablement program.
- Pilot 'onboarding buddy' pairing with senior ICs for first 30 days; track satisfaction.

End of notes. Will tidy and convert to shareable review deck.
